name: Fear of Man

counsel.text: The fear of God destroys the fear of man. The three children feared God, therefore they feared not the king's wrath. Dan 3: 16. The greater noise drowns the less; the noise of thunder drowns the noise of a river; so, when the fear of God is supreme in the soul, it drowns all other carnal fear.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the first commandment

counsel.text: It is better that God approve, than man applaud. The world may put us in their rubric and God put us in his black book. What is a man the better that his fellow-prisoners commend him, if his judge condemn him?
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Art of Divine Contentment, ch. 10

counsel.text: In particular, a man begins to be in repute for piety, wisdom, learning, or the like,--he is spoken of much to that purpose; his heart is tickled to hear of it, and his pride and ambition affected with it. If this man now, with all his strength, ply the things from whence his repute, and esteem, and glory amongst men do spring, with a secret eye to have it increased, he is entering into temptation; which, if he take not heed, will quickly render him a slave of lust.
counsel.author: John Owen

counsel.text: Some are naturally gentle, facile, easy to be entreated, pliable; which, though it be the noblest temper of nature, and the best and choicest ground, when well broken up and fallowed for grace to grow in, yet, if not watched over, will be a means of innumerable surprisals and entanglements in temptation.
counsel.author: John Owen

counsel.text: If Christ appears for us in heaven, then we must appear for him upon earth. Christ is not ashamed to carry our names on his breast, and shall we be ashamed of his truth? Does he plead our cause, and shall we not stand up in his cause?
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: A Body of Divinity, Christ's priestly office

counsel.text: It should be a Christian's ambition to wear his Saviour's livery, though it be sprinkled with blood and sullied with disgrace.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Art of Divine Contentment, ch. 10

counsel.text: Flesh only fears flesh; when the soul degenerates into carnal desires and delights, no wonder he falls into carnal fears. Have a care, Christian, thou bringest not thyself into bondage. Perhaps thy heart feeds on the applause of men, this will make thee afraid to be evil spoken of, as those who shuffled with Christ, John 12:42; owning him in private when they durst not confess him openly, for they loved the praise of men.
counsel.author: William Gurnall

counsel.text: Every man is most loath to fall into his hands whom he fears most. So that, if God hath once gained the supremacy of thy fear, thou wilt rather skip into the hottest fire the persecutor can make, than make God thy enemy.
counsel.author: William Gurnall

counsel.text: That God that hath always one hand to wipe away his children's tears from their eyes, that God hath always another hand to wipe off the dust that lies upon his children's names. Wronged innocency shall not long lie under a cloud.
counsel.author: Thomas Brooks
counsel.source: The Mute Christian Under the Smarting Rod

counsel.text: It is a mercy to be delivered from the praises of wicked men; wicked men's applauses oftentimes become the saints' reproaches.
counsel.author: Thomas Brooks
counsel.source: The Mute Christian Under the Smarting Rod

counsel.text: It is an evidence a man lives more to opinion and reputation of others than to conscience, when his grief is more for being disappointed of that approbation which he expects from men, than for his miscarriage towards God. It mars all in religion when we go about heavenly things with earthly affections, and seek not Christ in Christ, but the world.
counsel.author: Richard Sibbes
counsel.source: The Soul's Conflict with Itself, ch. 13

counsel.text: Undoubtedly, he that hath seen God once in the face of Christ, dares look the grimmest creature in the face, yea, death itself under any shape. The fear of all things flies before such a soul. Only a Christian is not ashamed of his confidence.
counsel.author: Richard Sibbes
counsel.source: The Soul's Conflict with Itself, ch. 33

prayers.title: A prayer of confession
prayers.text: Almighty God, you alone are to be feared, and the fear of you is the beginning of wisdom. I come through Jesus Christ. I confess that I have feared people more than you. I have kept silent when I should have spoken, and spoken when I should have kept silent. I have hidden my faith, bent the truth, and done what I knew was wrong, because I wanted to be liked or was afraid of being mocked. I have made the opinion of others my idol, and I have loved the praise of man more than the praise of God. The fear of man has been a snare to me, and it has made me a coward toward you and a flatterer toward them. Forgive me, Lord. Christ was not ashamed of me. He endured the cross, despising its shame, and he made the good confession before Pilate. For his sake pardon my cowardice. Holy Spirit, put this fear to death, and fill me with a holy fear of God that drives out the fear of man. Make me both bold and kind. I thank you that you are for me, so that no one can finally be against me, and that nothing can separate me from your love. In Jesus' name. Amen.

prayers.title: When I fear what they will think
prayers.text: Lord, I feel the pressure to please them, and I am tempted to hide or give way. Remind me now that you are my judge and my helper, and that their opinion does not decide my worth. You are on my side; I will not fear what man can do to me. Give me courage to do what is right and say what is true, with gentleness and respect. If I am mocked for Christ, let me count it an honor. Lord Jesus, you were despised and rejected for me; do not let me be ashamed of you. Holy Spirit, make me steady. Amen.

prayers.title: For a holy fear
prayers.text: Father, teach me to fear you rightly, with reverence and love, as your child who knows both your greatness and your goodness. Let your approval be enough for me. Free me from needing the applause of others and from dreading their frown. Make me faithful in small things when no one sees, and steady when everyone is watching. Give me a clear conscience before you and before others. Let me live for the day when my Master will say to me, Well done, good and faithful servant. Through Jesus Christ. Amen.

prayers.title: That we may not fear the reproach of men
prayers.text: Lord, teach us to endure hardness as good soldiers of Jesus Christ; that we may not fear the reproach of men, or their revilings, nor be ashamed of Christ or of his words, knowing whom we have believed, even one who is able to keep what we have committed to him against that day. Though bonds and afflictions should abide us, Lord, grant that none of these things may move us, and that we may not count life itself dear to us, so we may finish our course with joy. Enable us in all things to approve ourselves to God, and then to pass by honour and dishonour, by evil report and good report, clad with the armour of righteousness on the right hand and on the left, as those that account it a very small thing to be judged of man's judgment, for he that judgeth us is the Lord.
prayers.author: Matthew Henry

examinationQuestions: Whose approval did you most want today, and where did that desire lead you to say, or leave unsaid, what you should not have?
When you held back from owning Christ or speaking the truth, what were you afraid of losing, and why did it seem weightier than his favor?
Did you agree to anything today only to avoid someone's displeasure? What would faithfulness have looked like instead?
Do you change your words and manner to fit the room? What would change if God's verdict on you in Christ were enough?
Who has the power to unsettle you with a look or a word? Bring that person before God and ask where they have taken his place in your heart.
Is there a truth you need to speak, a wrong you need to confess, or a refusal you need to give, that you have put off out of fear?
fleeActions: Do the faithful thing you have been putting off for fear of someone: make the call, speak the truth kindly, or say no.
Before you walk into the room you dread, stop and pray that the fear of God would be greater in you than the fear of anyone there.
Open your Bible to Isaiah 51:12-13, read it, and then say aloud before God whom you have been fearing.
If you were silent about Christ when you should have spoken, go back to that person if you can, and tell them plainly and kindly that you belong to him.
Put your phone down and stop checking for replies and reactions. Go and do the work God has given you for this hour.
Tell a trusted believer in your church what you are afraid of, and ask them to pray that you would be faithful and bold.

afterFallReadings.text: Little did Peter think he should deny and forswear his Master so soon as ever he was questioned whether he knew him or no. It was no better when the hour of temptation came; all resolutions were forgotten, all love to Christ buried; the present temptation closing with his carnal fear carried all before it.
afterFallReadings.author: John Owen

afterFallReadings.text: Yea, let me add, that never any soul did or shall perish by the power of any lust, sin, or corruption, who could raise his soul by faith to an expectation of relief from Jesus Christ.
afterFallReadings.author: John Owen
afterFallReadings.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14
